---
title: "The browser viewer"
subtitle: "`index.html` and `src/viewer.ts`: watching the colony grow"
---

The browser version runs the same simulation as the command line, draws it on a canvas as it
runs, measures overlaps at every snapshot, and saves the recorded states. It is the
[live demo](simulation/index.html) of this site. It is a single static page with no server-side
code; [drawing](rendering.qmd) has its own chapter.

## The page

The page is a header with the controls and a status line, and a canvas that takes the rest of the
window.

```{.html file=index.html}
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Microfluidic Biofilm</title>
  <<page-style>>
</head>
<body>
  <<page-header>>
  <canvas id="canvas"></canvas>
  <<page-scripts>>
</body>
</html>
```

The layout is a column: the header wraps its controls onto several lines on narrow screens, and the
canvas fills the remaining height. Numbers use tabular figures so that the status line does not
jitter as they change; the overlap readout turns green or red against the target.

```{.html #page-style}
<style>
  body { margin: 0; font: 14px system-ui, sans-serif; background: #fff; color: #222; display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 100vh; }
  header { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px 16px; align-items: center; padding: 8px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd; }
  header h1 { font-size: 16px; margin: 0 8px 0 0; }
  button { font: inherit; padding: 3px 10px; }
  input[type=number] { width: 6em; font: inherit; }
  #status, #overlap { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #555; }
  #overlap.ok { color: #1a7f37; }
  #overlap.bad { color: #c62828; font-weight: 600; }
  select { font: inherit; }
  #canvas { flex: 1; width: 100%; min-height: 0; display: block; }
  kbd { border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 3px; padding: 0 4px; font-size: 12px; }
</style>
```

The controls: pause, single step and save (also on the keyboard: Space, N and J), the number of
steps per frame, the view, and the settings that apply when the simulation is restarted: the seed
(blank for a random one) and the snapshot interval. Then the status line, the overlap readout, a
reminder of the keys, and a link to this site.

```{.html #page-header}
<header>
  <h1>Microfluidic Biofilm</h1>
  <button id="pause" title="Space">Pause</button>
  <button id="step" title="N">Step</button>
  <button id="save" title="J">Save states…</button>
  <label>Steps/frame <input id="speed" type="number" min="1" max="200" value="1"></label>
  <label>View <select id="style">
    <option value="simple">Simple</option>
    <option value="diagnostic">Diagnostic (overlaps)</option>
  </select></label>
  <label>Seed <input id="seed" type="number" min="0" placeholder="random"></label>
  <label title="Steps between snapshots (multiple of 25); applies on Restart">Snapshot every <input id="snapshotInterval" type="number" min="25" step="25" value="300"> steps</label>
  <button id="restart" title="Restart with these settings (blank seed = random); unsaved states are lost">Restart</button>
  <span id="status"></span>
  <span id="overlap"></span>
  <span style="color:#888"><kbd>Space</kbd> pause · <kbd>N</kbd> step · <kbd>J</kbd> save</span>
  <a href="https://critalmediumblue.github.io/Rapier-for-bacteria/">How it works</a>
</header>
```

The compiled TypeScript imports Rapier by its npm package name, which a browser cannot resolve on
its own. An *import map* tells it where that file is: in the repository, inside `node_modules`;
the published site keeps the same path (`tools/build-site.sh` copies the file there). The viewer is
loaded as an ES module.

```{.html #page-scripts}
<script type="importmap">
  { "imports": { "@dimforge/rapier2d-simd-compat": "./node_modules/@dimforge/rapier2d-simd-compat/dist/rapier.mjs" } }
</script>
<script type="module" src="./build/viewer.js"></script>
```

## The viewer

`viewer.ts` is a plain script: it looks up the page's elements, reads the settings from the URL,
starts a simulation and drives it from the browser's animation frames.

```{.typescript file=src/viewer.ts}
<<viewer-imports>>

<<viewer-constants>>

<<viewer-file-handle>>

<<viewer-elements>>

<<viewer-url-settings>>

<<viewer-state>>

<<viewer-start>>

<<viewer-advance>>

<<viewer-frame>>

<<viewer-render>>

<<viewer-saving>>

<<viewer-controls>>

<<viewer-scripting>>

void startSimulation().then(() => requestAnimationFrame(frame));
```

```{.typescript #viewer-imports}
import { DEFAULT_PARAMS, SimulationParams } from "./model.js";
import { OVERLAP_TARGET_FRACTION, OVERLAP_WARMUP_STEPS, OverlapMeter, OverlapStats } from "./overlap.js";
import { ChamberRenderer, RENDER_STYLES, RenderStyle, ViewRect } from "./render.js";
import { Simulation, rapierVersion } from "./simulation.js";
```

The states are saved automatically every 500 snapshots. The diagnostic view highlights overlaps
deeper than 1% of the cell width: resting contacts always sit 0.1–0.5% deep (the solver's
tolerance), and highlighting those would colour the whole colony.

```{.typescript #viewer-constants}
const AUTO_SAVE_EVERY_SNAPSHOTS = 500;
const OVERLAP_VISIBLE_FRACTION = 0.01;
const STATES_FILE_NAME = "states.json";
```

### Elements and settings

Saving to a file the user picked uses the File System Access API, available in Chrome and Edge.
TypeScript's standard DOM types do not include it yet, so the few members used are declared here.

```{.typescript #viewer-file-handle}
interface WritableFileHandle {
  name: string;
  createWritable(): Promise<{ write(data: Blob): Promise<void>, close(): Promise<void> }>;
}
```

```{.typescript #viewer-elements}
const $ = <T extends HTMLElement>(id: string): T => document.getElementById(id) as T;
const canvas = $<HTMLCanvasElement>("canvas");
const renderer = new ChamberRenderer(canvas.getContext("2d")!);
const statusEl = $("status");
const overlapEl = $("overlap");
const pauseBtn = $<HTMLButtonElement>("pause");
const speedInput = $<HTMLInputElement>("speed");
const seedInput = $<HTMLInputElement>("seed");
const styleSelect = $<HTMLSelectElement>("style");
const snapshotInput = $<HTMLInputElement>("snapshotInterval");
```

Every setting can be given in the URL, so a particular run or view can be shared as a link, e.g.
`index.html?seed=7&speed=20&style=diagnostic&anchorMaxStretch=1`:

| URL parameter | Effect |
|---|---|
| `seed` | the random seed |
| `speed` | steps per frame |
| `style` | `simple` or `diagnostic` |
| `view` | `minX,minY,maxX,maxY`: zoom into a part of the chamber, e.g. `-50,185,-35,200` for the top-left corner |
| any model parameter | overrides its default, e.g. `snapshotInterval=600` |

Model parameters are recognised by their names in `DEFAULT_PARAMS`, as on the command line. The
seed, speed, style and snapshot interval are copied into the controls, where they can be changed
before a restart.

```{.typescript #viewer-url-settings}
const query = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const urlOverrides: Partial<SimulationParams> = {};
for (const [key, value] of query) {
  if (key in DEFAULT_PARAMS && value !== "" && !Number.isNaN(Number(value))) {
    (urlOverrides as Record<string, number>)[key] = Number(value);
  }
}
const urlStyle = query.get("style") as RenderStyle | null;
styleSelect.value = urlStyle && RENDER_STYLES.includes(urlStyle) ? urlStyle : "simple";
if (query.get("seed")) { seedInput.value = query.get("seed")!; }
if (query.get("speed")) { speedInput.value = query.get("speed")!; }
snapshotInput.value = String(urlOverrides.snapshotInterval ?? DEFAULT_PARAMS.snapshotInterval);
const viewParts = (query.get("view") ?? "").split(",").map(Number);
let view: ViewRect | undefined = viewParts.length === 4 && viewParts.every(Number.isFinite) && viewParts[0] < viewParts[2] && viewParts[1] < viewParts[3]
  ? { minX: viewParts[0], minY: viewParts[1], maxX: viewParts[2], maxY: viewParts[3] } : undefined;
```

### State

The viewer's state: the simulation (none while one is being created), whether it is paused, the
file being saved to, and counters for the speed readout. The overlap meter is shared between the
snapshot measurements and the diagnostic view. The diagnostic view's overlapping pairs are kept in
fixed arrays (up to 4096 pairs), and only re-measured when the simulation has moved.

```{.typescript #viewer-state}
let sim: Simulation | null = null;
let paused = false;
let saveHandle: WritableFileHandle | null = null;
let saving = false;
let lastSaveInfo = "not saved yet";
let rateSteps = 0, rateFrames = 0, rateStepMs = 0, rateDrawMs = 0, rateTime = performance.now();
let stepsPerSecond = 0, framesPerSecond = 0, stepMsPerFrame = 0, drawMsPerFrame = 0;
const meter = new OverlapMeter();
let lastOverlap: OverlapStats | null = null;
const pairs = { i: new Int32Array(4096), j: new Int32Array(4096), depth: new Float64Array(4096), count: 0 };
let pairsStep = -1;
```

A new simulation takes the URL's parameters, the snapshot interval and the seed from the controls.
If the parameters are invalid, the error appears in the status line.

```{.typescript #viewer-start}
async function startSimulation(): Promise<void> {
  const seedText = seedInput.value.trim();
  const overrides: Partial<SimulationParams> = { ...urlOverrides, snapshotInterval: Number(snapshotInput.value) };
  if (seedText !== "") { overrides.seed = Number(seedText); }
  try {
    sim = await Simulation.create(overrides);
  } catch (e) {
    statusEl.textContent = `could not start: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`;
    console.error(e);
    return;
  }
  lastOverlap = null;
  pairsStep = -1;
  console.log(`Simulation started: Rapier ${rapierVersion()}, seed ${sim.params.seed}`);
}
```

### The loop

`advance` runs a number of steps. At every snapshot it measures the overlaps for the readout and,
every 500 snapshots, saves. If the physics engine fails, the viewer pauses and says so; the
snapshots recorded until then can still be saved.

```{.typescript #viewer-advance}
function advance(steps: number): void {
  if (!sim) { return; }
  for (let i = 0; i < steps; i++) {
    let snapshotTaken: boolean;
    try {
      snapshotTaken = sim.step();
    } catch (e) {
      console.error(`The simulation failed at step ${sim.stepCount + 1}:`, e);
      if (!paused) { togglePause(); }
      lastSaveInfo = `SIMULATION FAILED at step ${sim.stepCount + 1} (see console); save with J to keep the snapshots`;
      return;
    }
    rateSteps++;
    if (snapshotTaken) {
      lastOverlap = meter.measure(sim, sim.params.radius, OVERLAP_TARGET_FRACTION * 2 * sim.params.radius);
      if (sim.states.snapshotCount % AUTO_SAVE_EVERY_SNAPSHOTS === 0) { void saveStates(true); }
    }
  }
}
```

Each animation frame advances the simulation by the chosen number of steps (1 to 200), then draws
it. The time spent on each is accumulated, and once a second the readout's averages are updated.
With a full chamber a step takes about 5 ms, so one step per frame leaves plenty of room in a
60 Hz frame, and more steps per frame trade smoothness for speed.

```{.typescript #viewer-frame}
function frame(): void {
  const t0 = performance.now();
  if (!paused) {
    const steps = Math.max(1, Math.min(200, Math.floor(Number(speedInput.value) || 1)));
    advance(steps);
  }
  const t1 = performance.now();
  render();
  const t2 = performance.now();
  rateStepMs += t1 - t0;
  rateDrawMs += t2 - t1;
  rateFrames++;
  if (t2 - rateTime >= 1000) {
    stepsPerSecond = (rateSteps * 1000) / (t2 - rateTime);
    framesPerSecond = (rateFrames * 1000) / (t2 - rateTime);
    stepMsPerFrame = rateStepMs / rateFrames;
    drawMsPerFrame = rateDrawMs / rateFrames;
    rateSteps = rateFrames = rateStepMs = rateDrawMs = 0;
    rateTime = t2;
  }
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}
```

### Drawing a frame

The canvas is sized in device pixels, so that lines stay sharp on high-resolution screens. In the
diagnostic view, the overlapping pairs deeper than 1% of the width are collected (once per step
the simulation has moved) and handed to the [renderer](rendering.qmd) together with the target
depth. Then the status line and the overlap readout are updated; during the warm-up the readout
explains why the overlaps are still large.

```{.typescript #viewer-render}
function render(): void {
  const dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1;
  const w = canvas.clientWidth, h = canvas.clientHeight;
  if (canvas.width !== Math.round(w * dpr) || canvas.height !== Math.round(h * dpr)) {
    canvas.width = Math.round(w * dpr);
    canvas.height = Math.round(h * dpr);
  }
  if (!sim) { return; }
  const style = styleSelect.value as RenderStyle;
  const radius = sim.params.radius;
  const targetDepth = OVERLAP_TARGET_FRACTION * 2 * radius;
  if (style === "diagnostic" && sim.stepCount !== pairsStep) {
    pairsStep = sim.stepCount;
    pairs.count = 0;
    const visible = OVERLAP_VISIBLE_FRACTION * 2 * radius;
    meter.measure(sim, radius, targetDepth, (i, j, depth) => {
      if (depth < visible || pairs.count === pairs.i.length) { return; }
      pairs.i[pairs.count] = i; pairs.j[pairs.count] = j; pairs.depth[pairs.count] = depth; pairs.count++;
    });
  }
  renderer.draw(sim, { style, radius, view, overlaps: style === "diagnostic" ? pairs : undefined, targetDepth });

  statusEl.textContent =
    `step ${sim.stepCount} · ${sim.cellCount} cells · ${sim.states.snapshotCount} snapshots · ` +
    `${stepsPerSecond.toFixed(0)} steps/s · ${framesPerSecond.toFixed(0)} fps ` +
    `(step ${stepMsPerFrame.toFixed(1)} ms + draw ${drawMsPerFrame.toFixed(1)} ms per frame) · ` +
    `seed ${sim.params.seed} · ${lastSaveInfo}`;
  if (lastOverlap) {
    const width = 2 * radius;
    const max = lastOverlap.maxDepth / width * 100, mean = lastOverlap.meanDepth / width * 100;
    const warmup = lastOverlap.step < OVERLAP_WARMUP_STEPS;
    overlapEl.textContent = `overlap at step ${lastOverlap.step}: max ${max.toFixed(1)}% · mean ${mean.toFixed(2)}% of cell width` +
      (warmup ? ` (warm-up: random initial placement relaxing until step ${OVERLAP_WARMUP_STEPS})` : ` (target < ${OVERLAP_TARGET_FRACTION * 100}%)`);
    overlapEl.className = warmup ? "" : max < OVERLAP_TARGET_FRACTION * 100 ? "ok" : "bad";
  } else {
    overlapEl.textContent = "overlap: measured at each snapshot";
    overlapEl.className = "";
  }
}
```

### Saving

A browser page cannot simply write to disk. There are two ways out:

- **Chrome and Edge** offer a file picker that returns a *handle* to a file of the user's choice.
  The first save asks for the file; later saves, including the automatic ones, overwrite it
  without asking.
- **Other browsers** can only download: the file is built as a `Blob` and offered as a download,
  as `states.json` when saved by hand and as numbered copies when saved automatically.

The `Blob` is built from the recorder's [pieces](recording.qmd#writing-the-file). Only one save
runs at a time; an automatic save that comes due during another is skipped.

```{.typescript #viewer-saving}
function buildBlob(): Blob {
  return new Blob(sim!.states.toPieces(), { type: "application/json" });
}

function download(blob: Blob, fileName: string): void {
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const link = document.createElement("a");
  link.download = fileName;
  link.href = url;
  link.click();
  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 60000);
}

async function saveStates(auto: boolean): Promise<void> {
  if (saving || !sim) { return; }
  saving = true;
  try {
    const blob = buildBlob();
    let target: string;
    if (saveHandle) {
      const writable = await saveHandle.createWritable();
      await writable.write(blob);
      await writable.close();
      target = saveHandle.name;
    } else {
      target = auto ? `states_${sim.states.snapshotCount}.json` : STATES_FILE_NAME;
      download(blob, target);
    }
    lastSaveInfo = `saved ${sim.states.snapshotCount} snapshots to ${target} at step ${sim.stepCount}`;
    console.log(`${lastSaveInfo} (${(blob.size / 1e6).toFixed(1)} MB)`);
  } catch (e) {
    lastSaveInfo = "save FAILED (see console)";
    console.error("Saving states failed:", e);
  } finally {
    saving = false;
  }
}

async function chooseFileAndSave(): Promise<void> {
  const picker = (window as any).showSaveFilePicker;
  if (picker && !saveHandle) {
    try {
      saveHandle = await picker({
        suggestedName: STATES_FILE_NAME,
        types: [{ description: "JSON", accept: { "application/json": [".json"] } }],
      });
    } catch {
      return;
    }
  }
  await saveStates(false);
}
```

### Controls

Stepping once pauses the simulation first. Restarting asks for confirmation if there are recorded
states, and forgets the file of the previous run, so that the new run does not overwrite it. Keys
typed into the input fields are left alone. Leaving the page with recorded states makes the
browser ask for confirmation.

```{.typescript #viewer-controls}
function togglePause(): void {
  paused = !paused;
  pauseBtn.textContent = paused ? "Resume" : "Pause";
}

function stepOnce(): void {
  if (!paused) { togglePause(); }
  advance(1);
}

async function restart(): Promise<void> {
  if (sim && sim.states.snapshotCount > 0 && !confirm("Restart the simulation? Unsaved states will be lost.")) { return; }
  sim = null;
  await startSimulation();
  saveHandle = null;
  lastSaveInfo = "not saved yet";
}

pauseBtn.addEventListener("click", togglePause);
$("step").addEventListener("click", stepOnce);
$("save").addEventListener("click", () => void chooseFileAndSave());
$("restart").addEventListener("click", () => void restart());
window.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  if (e.target instanceof HTMLInputElement || e.target instanceof HTMLSelectElement) { return; }
  switch (e.key) {
    case " ": e.preventDefault(); togglePause(); break;
    case "n": case "N": stepOnce(); break;
    case "j": case "J": void chooseFileAndSave(); break;
  }
});
window.addEventListener("beforeunload", (e) => {
  if (sim && sim.states.snapshotCount > 0) { e.preventDefault(); }
});
```

### Scripting

`window.biofilm` makes the viewer usable from the browser console or from a headless browser, e.g.
to take screenshots at given steps. It exposes the simulation, the latest overlap measurement and
the timing, and lets a script pause, resume, advance, zoom (`setView({minX, minY, maxX, maxY})`, or
no argument for the whole chamber) and download the states without the file picker.

```{.typescript #viewer-scripting}
(window as any).biofilm = {
  get sim() { return sim; },
  get overlap() { return lastOverlap; },
  get timing() { return { stepsPerSecond, framesPerSecond, stepMsPerFrame, drawMsPerFrame }; },
  download: (fileName: string = STATES_FILE_NAME) => { if (sim) { download(buildBlob(), fileName); } },
  pause: () => { if (!paused) { togglePause(); } },
  resume: () => { if (paused) { togglePause(); } },
  advance,
  setView: (rect?: ViewRect) => { view = rect; },
};
```
